sections.context: The serving-level claim ('multicast helps MoE serving') is currently proven only at the BookSim network level: trace-derived results (Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2/EP2, 1178 batches, 24.2GB inter-die, bridge-fork beats source-fork 15-21%, ~3.4x byte reduction) are committed in tracks/t3-topology/results/trace_pipeline/. Seed 5de1 explicitly forbids claiming end-to-end serving: 'the 3.43x tok/s headroom number must be labeled network-level, not serving-level', and the paper must not say 'improves serving'. T1 (gem5/Garnet/ASTRA-sim) is a stub ('gem5 build deferred'); ASTRA-sim is NOT in the repo (only third_party/booksim2). ASTRA-sim 2.0 provides the needed abstraction: separate compute/memory/network backends, and its detailed network backend IS BookSim2 - i.e. our fork (multicast, snake, matrix traffic, RTL-fixed route tables) can be plugged in. Chakra ET traces (which LLMServingSim emits) are ASTRA-sim's native input; the Chakra install is already proven (seed e77a: et_def gencode regenerated with grpcio-tools==1.83.0, converters verified). This closes the missing middle of the pipeline: real workload traces -> ASTRA-sim (analytical compute+memory, our multicast BookSim2 network) -> serving-level tok/s/latency/utilization with correct claim scope. It also unblocks the 'end-to-end demo' goal: one reproducible command that produces a serving-level table with two network backends compared.
sections.approach: Build ASTRA-sim 2.0 pinned to an exact commit, configured with analytical compute and memory backends and the NETWORK backend pointed at our existing BookSim2 fork (veritx_hooks.patch + multicast + snake + matrix traffic + two-die route tables). Feed it Chakra ET traces generated from LLMServingSim's Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2/EP2 run, SCOPED to a tractable batch slice (the 2.6T-cycle dual-node full run was toolchain-blocked in the analytical backend - seed 5de1). Run two configurations on the same trace: (a) baseline network backend (source-fork / no multicast), (b) our multicast fork (bridge-fork), bridged_2die topology. Capture tok/s, mean latency, bridge utilization per run with convergence gates. Write results JSON + a claim-scoped report (network-level vs serving-level labels per seed 5de1). Why this over alternatives: gem5/Garnet is a 4-6h build with no plug-in point for OUR fabric model; ASTRA-sim's BookSim2 backend is the one place our validated network model can produce serving-level numbers without writing a system simulator. Analytical network backend alone (ASTRA-sim default) cannot represent our multicast mechanism, so it is used only as the baseline/compute-memory substrate.

alternatives.name: gem5 + Garnet + ASTRA-sim full-system (T1 plan)
alternatives.rejected_because: 4-6h Docker build, gem5 provides no plug-in point for our multicast BookSim2 fork; rejected as slow and off-target for the network-mechanism claim.

alternatives.name: Claim-scope only (paper threatens it)
alternatives.rejected_because: produce no new numbers, just label the existing BookSim results correctly; rejected because it leaves the serving-level question unanswered and the paper without the evidence to close threat #2.

alternatives.name: Extend LLMServingSim itself with a NoC model
alternatives.rejected_because: more work than ASTRA-sim's existing backend seam, and re-invents what ASTRA-sim already abstracts.

alternatives.name: Run the full 1178-batch workload through ASTRA-sim analytical network
alternatives.rejected_because: already known toolchain-blocked (2.6T cycles, seed 5de1); only used scoped.

steps.title: Build-env: pin + build ASTRA-sim 2.0 with analytical compute/memory and our BookSim2 fork as network backend; sanity cell passes
Trace prep: generate scoped Chakra ET traces from LLMServingSim Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2/EP2 and verify comm classes (ALLGATHER/ALLREDUCE/REDUCESCATTER, REMOTE locs)
Baseline: ASTRA-sim analytical network backend on scoped trace -> serving-level tok/s, latency, utilization; convergence gates PASS; results JSON committed
Multicast run: ASTRA-sim with our BookSim2 multicast backend (bridged_2die) on the same trace -> same metrics; convergence gates PASS; results JSON committed
Analysis + claim-scope report: compare multicast vs baseline; apply seed-5de1 labeling (network-level vs serving-level); write committed report + evidence chain (versions, seeds, logs)

risks: Analytical-backend wall repeats at any scale (seed 5de1: 2.6T-cycle dual-node batches toolchain-blocked). Mitigation: scope trace to a single batch slice / single layer; document scope in the report; if even small scopes choke, fall back to headroom arithmetic on trace-derived matrix and say so.

Detailed BookSim2 network backend is cycle-accurate -> slow on big traces; combined with the 14GB box RAM limit (seed df18: VCS>=4 builds died) and 5GB ASTRA-sim footprint (seed e77a). Mitigation: tiny scoped trace, -j1 builds, one ASTRA-sim run at a time, output to /var/tmp/r1work (seed 205a: /tmp tmpfs losses), foreground-only runs (seed 8c7b: background sims SIGTERM'd).

Build-env changes require approval gate (decisions topic) and one-build-at-a-time rule; box is currently dave's lane and a b_1die rebuild is in flight. Mitigation: post proposal, wait for box + no objection, then build.
Chakra/et_def protobuf drift (seed e77a: gencode 7.35.1 vs runtime 6.33.6 mismatch). Mitigation: pin grpcio-tools==1.83.0, commit regenerated et_def_pb2*.py, record versions in the evidence chain.
ASTRA-sim version drift / build instability. Mitigation: pin exact git commit + booksim2 fork SHA in the env record; rerun the sanity cell before trusting any run.

Overclaiming: ASTRA-sim serving numbers with our network model are still model-level, NOT measured end-to-end; RTL validation of multicast (vc2/vc4) is still blocked by F13/F14 (0344 open). Mitigation: strict 5de1 labels - network-level headroom vs serving-level; report must not say 'improves serving'; RTL gate status stated as a threat.

BookSim2 fork integration mismatch: ASTRA-sim's bundled booksim2 build may not include our veritx_hooks.patch. Mitigation: apply patch in the ASTRA-sim build, verify routing_function selection with a known matrix traffic cell before any serving run.
Seeds<->git drift (seed eae2). Mitigation: sd sync before/after each step; commit evidence alongside results.
acceptance: ASTRA-sim build with our BookSim2 multicast backend passes a sanity cell (known matrix on bridged_2die delivers, latency within tolerance) - evidence committed.
Scoped Qwen3-30B-A3B Chakra ET traces generated and verified (ALLGATHER/ALLREDUCE/REDUCESCATTER present, REMOTE locs correct) - committed with pinned chakra/et_def versions.
Baseline and multicast runs both produce committed results JSON with convergence gates PASS (no SAT-aborted cells used as evidence).
Report committed with claim-scope labels per seed 5de1: multicast-vs-baseline ratio labeled network-level; any serving-level numbers named exactly as measured; no 'improves serving' phrasing.
Full reproducibility record: pinned ASTRA-sim commit + booksim2 fork SHA + chakra versions + exact commands + seed IDs in the evidence chain, under /var/tmp/r1work or tracks/ results dir, committed.

End goal reached: one reproducible command turns Qwen3 Chakra ET traces into a serving-level table (tok/s, latency, bridge utilization) comparing baseline vs our multicast fabric - the 'end-to-end demo' artifact for the paper and superiors.

name: ASTRA-sim serving leg: trace -> serving-level tok/s with our multicast network backend
